reframing_when: The question asks 'how should we do X' without asking 'should we be doing X at all given what else we could do with the same resources' — the displaced alternative is invisible.
The question treats a continuation or default path as free when the real cost is the best alternative use of the same resources, attention, or time.
The question frames the decision in terms of explicit costs only and suppresses the implicit costs — the non-financial opportunity costs (optionality, learning, trust) are hidden.
reframing_move: Surface the displaced alternative: ask 'compared to what?' — the question shifts from 'should we do X' to 'what is the best alternative use of the same resources, and is X better than that?'
curation_note: Opportunity-cost reframes by making invisible displaced alternatives visible. The source is explicit on 'Compared to what?' as the seminal reframing question, implicit vs explicit cost distinction, and the sponge-vs-sieve metaphor. Strongest on counterfactual suppression and commitment escalation.

reframing_when.note: Three activations from source material: displaced-alternative blindness, free-continuation illusion, and suppressed implicit costs.

frame_patterns_challenged.note: Counterfactual suppression is the primary target ('compared to what?'). Commitment escalation via continuation-as-free illusion. Proxy optimization via explicit-cost-only framing. Scope lock via narrow resource-boundary definition.
